{{Quote|Gamorr can put a boar on Pzob, but we can't&hellip;|Common expression for when a seemingly easy task could not be accomplished|<ref name="TEA" />}}
'''Pzob''' was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Herios sector/Legends|Herios sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], settled by [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorreans]] from the world of [[Gamorr/Legends|Gamorr]] a long period of [[Time/Legends|time]] prior to the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. The settlers, organized into various clans, constantly waged war on each other. All other concerns were secondary to the fighting, and as a result Pzob's inhabitants had a nearly non-existent relationship with advanced technology. The planet was covered in dark, dense forests with tall [[Tree/Legends|trees]], an environment that greatly appealed to the colonists. Pzob's remote location, combined with the relative primitiveness of its inhabitants, led to it being considered a backwater world. However, this also contributed to the planet going untouched by all major [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] conflicts.

The [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] established a [[Pzob stormtrooper base|secret military base]] on Pzob in [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]], intending to use the [[Troop/Legends|troops]] stationed there to man the ''[[Eye of Palpatine]]'', an enormous [[Warship/Legends|warship]]. However, the [[Starship/Legends|ship]] was [[Saboteur/Legends|sabotaged]] by [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], and the [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] on Pzob were left to their own devices. Nearly all of them were eventually [[Death/Legends|killed]] in either internal fighting, or in Gamorrean attacks. When the ''Eye of Palpatine'' was re-activated in [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], several of the Gamorrean colonists&mdash;along with the [[Triv Pothman|sole surviving Imperial soldier]]&mdash;were captured by the ship's automated security systems.

==Description==
{{Quote|Only after I was living in the forest on Pzob I realized how much I loved it, how much I'd missed the woods and the trees of Chandrila.|Triv Pothman, reminiscing about his homeworld|<ref name="CotJ" />}}
Pzob, located in the [[K749 system]] of the [[Herios sector/Legends|Herios sector]]<ref name="TEAOC" /> in the south-eastern [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]],<ref name="TEGPM" /> was a remote [[Planet/Legends|world]], far from most [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]].<ref name="TEA" /> It was covered in thick forests of tall [[Tree/Legends|trees]] with leathery leaves, somewhat reminiscent of the rainforests of the planet [[Ithor/Legends|Ithor]]. Most of the vegetation on the planet was dark [[Color/Legends|blue]]-green, and the light from Pzob's [[K749 system's star|sun]] bathed the environment in a golden hue. The planet's climate was temperate, and the [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] was breathable for both [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorreans]] and [[Human/Legends|Humans]].<ref name="CotJ" />

Between [[52 BBY/Legends|52]] and [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the area of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] containing Pzob was considered to be part of [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]].<ref name="TEA" /> Apart from the presence of a [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] [[Pzob stormtrooper base|base]] during the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]],<ref name="CSWEPzob" /> no major [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] power had anything to do with Pzob.<ref name="TEAn1">Based on Pzob's location on political maps throughout ''[[The Essential Atlas]]''.</ref> The remoteness of the Gamorrean colony led to it&mdash;at times&mdash;being cited as an example of a backwater world, out of touch with the rest of the [[galactic community]].<ref name="Star by Star">''[[The New Jedi Order: Star by Star]]''</ref>

==History==
{{Quote|The Gamorreans haven't stopped fighting each other long enough to set up a technological base of any kind on any planet where they've settled.|Luke Skywalker|<ref name="CotJ" />}}
The [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] discovered the world between [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000]] and [[3000 BBY]],<ref name="TEA" /> and assigned it the [[Galactic Registry]] number 011-733-800-022.<ref name="CotJ" /> Pzob was settled by Gamorreans from the nearby planet [[Gamorr/Legends|Gamorr]] generations<ref name="TEGPM" /> prior to [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]].<ref name="CSWEPzob" /> This was considered unusual, as Gamorreans were not traditionally a colonizing [[Species/Legends|species]],<ref name="TEA" /> nor were they renowned for their expertise in manufacturing advanced [[Starship/Legends|starships]].<ref name="NEGAS">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> The settlers organized themselves into clans, and started waging war on each other.<ref name="TEGPM" /> The constant feuding had an adverse effect on the technological development of the settlers, which meant that advanced technology was not commonplace on Pzob. The planet was rarely visited, with the last official report on Pzob being filed some [[Time/Legends|time]].<ref name="CotJ" />

Later, the Galactic Empire established a temporary<ref name="TEGPM" /> military base on Pzob with a crew of forty-five [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]], not far from the territories of the Gamorrean [[Gakfedd tribe|Gakfedd]] and [[Klagg tribe|Klagg clans]]. This was part of a series of secret bases set up to eventually man the ''[[Eye of Palpatine]]'', an enormous [[Battleship/Legends|battleship]] commissioned by [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]].<ref name="TEGPM" /> Relations between the stormtroopers and the Gamorrean clans were peaceful at first, with the Imperial soldiers welcome to visit native pubs.<ref name="DS">[[Death Star (novel)|''Death Star'']]</ref> Before long, however, the warlike nature of the local Gamorreans<ref name="CotJ" /> prompted them to field a series of skirmishes against the stormtrooper base.<ref name="CSWEPzob" /> The Gamorrean brothers [[Thok (Gamorrean guard)/Legends|Thok]] and [[Gorc]] of the [[Skunnt]] clan grew up on Pzob, and the [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] pair discovered their powers when Thok belched a ball of fire into the snout of his rival [[Scumbo/Legends|Scumbo]]. Believing that they would be able to use their powers to make their fortunes, Thok took his brother offworld.<ref name="Barely">{{SW|url=news/barely-tolerable-alien-henchmen-of-the-empire-part-2|series=Barely Tolerable: Alien Henchmen of the Empire|text=Part 2|nolive=1}}</ref>

[[File:Pzobbase.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The ruins of the stormtrooper base on Pzob]]
As the wait for the ''Eye of Palpatine'' grew longer and ammunition ran low, the stormtroopers were all [[Death/Legends|killed]] by either Gamorreans or through internal fighting. The only exception was [[Triv Pothman]], who was captured by the Gakfedd clan. He served that tribe for two years, followed by a year of servitude to the Klagg clan, but eventually escaped and took to living in the ruins of the stormtrooper base.<ref name="CotJ" />

The ''Eye of Palpatine'' did not arrive until much later, having been halted for several years by [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] interference. However, the Imperial sympathizer [[Irek Ismaren]] was able to re-activate the ship, prompting it to continue its original programming. This included picking up all of its contingents of stormtroopers on various Outer Rim worlds, which included Pzob. Arriving on the planet, the ''Eye of Palpatine'' was assaulted by Gamorreans, which caused it to activate security measures, capturing Pothman, members of the Gakfedd and Klagg clans, as well as the Jedi [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] who was present on the planet to investigate a [[Disturbance in the Force/Legends|disturbance in the Force]]. The large ship was destroyed shortly afterward, above the planet [[Belsavis/Legends|Belsavis]].<ref name="CotJ" />

==Inhabitants==
[[File:GamorreanBoarAndSow-EGPM.jpg|thumb|Two Gamorreans from Pzob]]
{{Main|Gamorrean/Legends}}
Gamorreans were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] species of porcine [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]], known for their cultural focus on battle. The green-skinned species sported prominent horns and tusks, and was organized in strict matriarchal societies.<ref name="NEGAS" />

Pzob was the sole colony of the Gamorrean [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of Gamorr.<ref name="TEA" /> The thick forests were of particular appeal to the species.<ref name="CotJ" /> The settlers arrived several generations prior to the start of the Imperial Period,<ref name="CSWEPzob" /> and soon started feuding amongst each other. Two prominent factions were the rival Gakfedd and Klagg clans. Warfare was a constant in the Gamorrean settlers' culture, and other concerns, such as technological development, were deemed to be less important. This focus on the clan war led to a very technologically simple society, which meant that [[Droid/Legends|droids]] were not welcome in the Gamorrean settlements.<ref name="CotJ" />

===Fauna===
The [[feathered lizard]], a small turquoise reptile, was native to Pzob. Also present was a species of [[Pzob bipedal creature|forest-dwelling bipeds]] roughly the height of an adult Human knee.<ref name="CotJ" />

==Locations==
The Galactic Empire's military base was located particularly close to the Klagg clan's village,<ref name="TEGPM" /> but also in proximity to the settlement of the Gakfedd clan.<ref name="CotJ" /> A location of some importance was the [[Pzob Forest Battle Yard]], an arena-like structure where Gamorrean fighters could duel.<ref name="TEGPM" />

==Behind the scenes==
Pzob first appeared in the novel [[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']] ([[1995]]) by [[Barbara Hambly]]. ''[[The Essential Guide to Planets and Moons]]'' ([[1998]]) included an entry for the planet, fleshing out a few more details. The planet was featured in the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']] (1998), which did not expand upon the planet; in fact, Pzob was represented with a generic planet model within the game. Pzob's location was finally pinpointed in ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' ([[2009]]). ''Atlas'' author [[Jason Fry]] included a mention of Pzob in the planet entry for Gamorr, as a humorous aside to illustrate the unlikeliness of Gamorr establishing a colony world.<ref name="blog">{{Blog|danwallace|145|Endnotes for Star Wars: The Essential Atlas (part 3 of 5)}}</ref>

===Conflicting sources===
The PC game ''Star Wars: Rebellion'' mistakenly places Pzob in the [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell sector]]. [[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion|''The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion]] lists a "Pzob system" instead of the K749 system.
